label: rem:spectrahedral-phase-collapse-prior-art
title: Prior art for spectrahedral rank-drop boundaries, moment hierarchies, and conic phase transitions
html:
The determinant locus and facial rank drop analyzed for the auxiliary z_{\mathrm{aux}} = \sqrt{q}/(q+1) Gram pencil in Spectrahedral collapse and conformal rigidity---together with the permanent rank-5 Temperley–Lieb quotient geometry at z = q^3/(q^2+1)---belong to a general convex-algebraic mechanism studied across algebraic optimization, quantum many-body physics, and high-dimensional conic geometry.

Algebraic boundaries and theta-body hierarchies of spectrahedra

In convex algebraic geometry, Cynthia Vinzant [vinzant2014] characterizes the boundary of a spectrahedron \{x : G(x) \succeq 0\} through the determinantal hypersurface \det G(x) = 0 and its stratified singular locus, where the positive-semidefinite pencil drops rank and the feasible region collapses onto a lower-dimensional face. João Gouveia, Pablo A. Parrilo, and Rekha R. Thomas [gouveia-parrilo-thomas2010] introduced theta bodies of polynomial ideals to govern when projected spectrahedral relaxations collapse exactly onto the convex hull of an algebraic variety, while Monique Laurent [laurent2009] and Christine Bachoc and Frank Vallentin [bachoc-vallentin2008] developed symmetry-adapted moment and semidefinite hierarchies on rank-deficient invariant Gram cones. At z = q^3/(q^2+1), where the q-antisymmetriser lies in the Gram radical for every q, positivity acts natively on the five-dimensional quotient cone rather than through a scalar determinant root.

Reduced-density-matrix faces, bootstrap kinks, and conic thresholds

In variational quantum mechanics, Valentin Zauner, David Draxler, Laurens Vanderstraeten, Jutho Haegeman, and Frank Verstraete [zauner-verstraete2016] showed that symmetry-breaking and critical phase boundaries coincide with singular rank-drop faces of projected reduced-density-matrix spectrahedra. The same facial boundary mechanism drives the extremal-functional kinks of Sheer El-Showk, Miguel F. Paulos, David Poland, Slava Rychkov, David Simmons-Duffin, and Alessandro Vichi [elshowk2012, simmons-duffin2015] in conformal field theory, as well as the confinement--deconfinement Gram rank-drop walls identified in lattice gauge bootstraps by Vladimir Kazakov and Zechuan Zheng [kazakov-zheng2023]. In conic integral geometry, David L. Donoho and Jared Tanner [donoho-tanner2009] and Dennis Amelunxen, Martin Lotz, Michael B. McCoy, and Joel A. Tropp [amelunxen-lotz-mccoy-tropp2014] proved that sharp feasibility thresholds in linear and semidefinite programs are governed by facial projection counts and statistical dimension---a finite-dimensional geometric transition certified algebraically by exact rational dual multipliers and strict complementary slackness.
